access_notes: Viewed 2026-11-08. Painted 1830; the museum's title calls him Sauk and the 1812 native research (native.json) records the museum's description of the sitter as Potawatomi of the Prairie Band. Seen: black hair cut loose at the jaw, a red blanket round the shoulders, strings of beads, broad dark wrist bands, painted lines on the body. A man at prayer in a sitting, not everyday dress at Chicago.
what_it_supplies: a Great Lakes man's loose, jaw-length black hair and a blanket over the shoulders, painted from life in 1830
what_it_does_not_supply: a settled nation for the sitter: the title says Sauk
